overview: Art therapists use drawing, painting and other creative work to help clients express feelings, cope with trauma and build skills. They run sessions, talk with clients to build trust, and write treatment plans and progress reports. O*NET rates knowledge of therapy and counseling at 5 out of 5 for this job, psychology at 4.97 and fine arts at 4.51. Most positions need a master's degree in art therapy and a credential. BLS publishes pay only for a broader therapists group, with a median of $77,930. The work offers a lot of freedom but can involve conflict and emotional strain.
pay: BLS does not publish pay for art therapists alone, so these figures are for the broader “Therapists, All Other” group. Its median is $77,930, with the middle half earning $58,850 to $105,760. New Jersey has the most of these jobs, 7,090, with a median of $100,250, 29% above the national figure.

faq.q: How much do art therapists make?
faq.a: BLS reports pay for the broader "Therapists, All Other" group: a May 2025 median of $77,930. The lowest 10% earn under $46,540 and the top 10% earn $152,530 or more. The District of Columbia ($127,010) and Illinois ($116,200) have the highest state medians.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be an art therapist?
faq.a: Most art therapists need a master's degree in art therapy, which combines studio art with psychology and supervised clinical hours. O*NET places the job in Job Zone 5. There are 10 related majors, including art therapy, music therapy and dance therapy, and many states also require a license.

faq.q: What skills do art therapists need?
faq.a: O*NET rates active listening, speaking and monitoring at 4 out of 5 for this job, and writing at 3.75 for treatment notes. Strong artistic interest also matters: the artistic score is 5.49 out of 7, next to a social score of 5.64.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to art therapist?
faq.a: The closest are Marriage and Family Therapists (89% match), mental health and substance abuse social workers (84%) and Healthcare Social Workers (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Marriage and Family Therapists earn a median of $66,940 and need a similar master's degree and license.
